l01: Everyone asks Claude for the prompt that makes viral videos. There isn't one.
l02: This whole video was made by Claude. The script, every frame, every sound.
l03: Even this voice is a model trained on mine.
l04: So here are seven rules that make AI video look directed, not generated.
l05: Rule one. Stop prompting. Start directing.
l06: Ask for a cool motion video and you get slop. Give it a director's notes and you get a film.
l07: Claude does most of the work. Your idea and your taste are the part it can't fake.
l08: Rule two. Write your style down once.
l09: Fonts, colours, where the text sits, how every word moves in. Then turn that guide into a skill.
l10: Now Claude never has to guess, and you never explain it twice.
l11: Rule three. Plan every line before a single frame.
l12: Script on the left, the scene on the right. Captions, a small UI, half screen, or full screen.
l13: You decide what pops up and when. That's the part Claude can't see.
l14: Rule four. Record the voice first, then animate to it.
l15: Whisper gives every word a timestamp, so each cut lands right on a spoken word.
l16: Rule five. Small, calm, and on the beat.
l17: Words rise in one at a time, in under a second and a half. Cut every two to three seconds.
l18: Make every element twenty five percent smaller, and trade pure colours for duller ones. It instantly looks more expensive.
l19: Rule six. Sound is half the video.
l20: Whooshes for movement. Clicks and pops for things that appear. Risers and hits for the big reveal.
l21: Put the whoosh's peak on the fastest frame. One big hit per scene. And nothing ever covers the voice.
l22: Voice on top, music twelve decibels under it, ducked under every word.
l23: Rule seven. Watch it like a director.
l24: Pull a still at every hit. Is the text clear? Does the sound land on the move? Then give notes, and let Claude rebuild.
l25: And check every fact against the source. One wrong number kills a good video.
l26: One editor timed his whole edit. Almost two hours, and he only worked twenty minutes of it.
l27: So the prompt was never the secret. The direction is.
